"A" and "B", and;

Hold that, the actions of the Respondent No.1 Police in registering the compliant of the Respondent No.2 in Crime No. 204/2022 Sri. Sujesh Pachiriyan vs State Of Karnataka on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161119551/
2 and immediately commencing the investigation, without preliminary inquiry, are in violation of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Lalita Kumari v/s Government of Uttar Pradesh and others, (2014) 2 SCC 1 and in Arnesh Kumar v. 2. Heard Sri.Amar Correa, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, Sri.B.N.Jagadeesha, learned Addl. SPP appearing for respondent No.1, Sri.B.K.Mohan, learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 and have perused the material on record.
3. During the subsistence of the said petition, in a matrimonial appeal before the High Court of Kerala, parties to the lis have settled the dispute by drawing up certain terms of settlement.

The settlement reads as follows:
"MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT UNDER SECTION 89 OF THE CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE READ WITH RULES 24 & 25 OF THE KERALA CIVIL PROCEDURE (MEDIATION), RULES, 2008:-
NC: 2026:KHC:6546 HC-KAR 1.
The above Mat Appeal No.966/2025 is filed challenging the Judgment dated 3/09/2025 in OP No.238/2021 on the files of Family Court, Kasaragod.
2. The above Mat Appeal No.1097/2025 is filed challenging the Judgment dated 3/09/2025 in OP No.325/2021 on the files of Family Court, Kasaragod.
3. OP No. 238/2021 was filed by Mr.Sujesh Pachiriyan/1st respondent seeking to declare him as the guardian of his daughter Abheri.
4. OP No.325/2021 was filed by Mr.Sujesh Pachiriyan/1st respondent seeking divorce from Shruthi R/Appellant.
5. The mother of the Appellant Sheela P., herein after be referred as 2nd respondent in Mat Appeal No.1097/2025.

6. The matter has been settled between the parties on the following terms:-
i) The 1st respondent will be the legal guardian of the daughter Abheri till she attains her majority.

However, Abheri will be with the permanent custody of her mother i.e,
the appellant.

sentences.text: The appellant shall provide access to the respondents 1 and 2, to contact Abheri as and when required, through Video calls or phone calls.

iii) As the 1st respondent is presently employed in United States of America and is planning to come back to India during March 2026, the appellant shall not object the 1st respondent in meeting Abheri on Saturdays and Sundays, after the 1st respondent arrives in India.
The venue of meeting will be mutually decided by the parties at the relevant time.
iv) The appellant hereby undertakes that she will not oppose if Abheri intends to stay overnight with the 1st respondent.
This arrangement is agreed between the parties, applies during the period of School Vacations also which includes Pooja Holidays, Winter Holidays during December and Summer Holidays.
